title: US appeals court clears Perplexity’s shopping agent to act for users on Amazon
friendlyTitle: A US court lets Perplexity’s shopping agent return to Amazon
summary: The Ninth Circuit vacated an injunction that had blocked Perplexity’s Comet shopping agent from Amazon. The court held that the browser did not itself access Amazon’s servers under the relevant computer-crime-law theory when it acted through an authorised user.
friendlySummary: The court removed an order that stopped Perplexity’s browser agent from shopping on Amazon for users.
whyItMatters: The decision gives browser agents more room to perform tasks on a person’s behalf, at least under this legal theory and at this stage of the case. Platforms, agent makers and users still need clear rules for consent, identity, purchasing authority and error handling.
friendlyWhyItMatters: AI helpers may get more freedom to use websites for you. Clear permission and spending limits are still important.
